audit_findings.title: Sustaining fleet investment may be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 rental-equipment and PP&E purchases were $186.956m gross and $103.327m net of $83.629m used-equipment proceeds, versus the $142.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated maintenance-capex deduction raises recurring owner earnings and every scenario derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant capital expenditures are required to maintain and grow the Company’s rental assets.
audit_findings.explanation: No maintenance-capex error is demonstrated because the filed purchases include both maintenance and growth. Nevertheless, the expenditure base is comparable to or larger than the anchor, capitalized refurbishments were $19.4m, and first-half 2026 rental-equipment purchases rose to $124.038m. A plausible reclassification of only part of this spending could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild fleet-level maintenance capex using unit age, utilization, disposals, replacement prices and capitalized refurbishments; reconcile it to gross purchases and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Historical interest may understate the current debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest-quarter interest expense of $7.113m annualizes to $28.452m, $2.170m below FY2025 interest expense of $30.622m and equal to 1.5% of the $142.7m anchor before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level owner-earnings DCF, recurring interest expense reduces owner earnings rather than debt being deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense decreased $16.6 million, due to 23% lower average debt levels of the Company, accompanied by 15% lower net average interest rates of 5.48% in 2025 compared to 6.48% in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The alleged current understatement is not demonstrated. Despite $589.895m of quarter-end debt, the latest quarter's 4.95% effective rate produced an annualized interest burden below FY2025 expense. The observed difference is small relative to the anchor and points toward slight understatement, not overstatement, of value from using FY2025 interest. Future variable-rate changes remain possible but are not a present valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the forward run rate from the $399.895m revolving balance, fixed-note coupons, commitment fees and post-quarter borrowing rates; rerun only if normalized annual interest differs materially from approximately $28.5m-$30.6m.

audit_findings.title: The trend anchor may mix different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $485.9m of filed acquisition spending in 2023 and 2025, plus the $268.0m Adler Tanks sale price in 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Perimeter changes alter the historical owner-earnings series, the $142.7m trend anchor and the distinction between organic growth and acquisition-funded growth.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2023, the company transacted a total of $23.8 million and $462.1 million in acquisition related costs, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated comparability defect: the valuation reports no defined perimeter while fitting a long trend across major acquisitions and a divestiture. The direction is mixed because acquired earnings without acquisition outlays can overstate sustainable owner earnings or growth, while disposed earnings or conservative trend effects can work the other way. The transaction scale is plainly capable of changing the anchor and valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Restate each trend year to the current continuing-business perimeter, separate acquired from organic owner earnings, charge recurring acquisition spending where required, and rerun the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized cloud implementation spending may escape the capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.4m capitalized in 2025, equal to 8.0% of the $142.7m anchor; omitted recurring portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted maintenance portion should reduce owner earnings as an operating cash investment even though accounting expense is deferred.
audit_findings.evidence: There was $ 11.4 million in cloud computing arrangements capitalized to prepaid expenses and other assets for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash investment is filed and large enough to matter if it recurs, but the record does not show whether the owner-earnings calculation already deducted it or what portion is sustaining rather than temporary implementation spending. Therefore an error and its material recurring amount remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $11.4m cash payment through the 2025 owner-earnings worksheet, identify maintenance versus one-time implementation costs, and rerun all scenarios using the normalized recurring deduction.

audit_findings.title: Rental-equipment sale proceeds and gains require matched treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 used-equipment proceeds were $83.629m, the accounting gain was $44.191m, and rental-equipment purchases were $142.576m
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings must remove the accounting gain once, include disposal cash once, and pair proceeds with gross sustaining fleet purchases.
audit_findings.evidence: Sales of rental equipment occur routinely as a normal part of the Company’s rental businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: No mismatched treatment is demonstrated because the detailed owner-earnings reconciliation was not supplied. The filed amounts are nevertheless material relative to the $142.7m anchor: double-counting the gain could overstate value, while omitting proceeds after deducting gross purchases could understate it. Inconsistent replacement assumptions could also overstate sustainable value.
audit_findings.action: Produce a line-by-line 2025 reconciliation from net income to owner earnings showing removal of the $44.191m gain, inclusion of the $83.629m proceeds and separation of maintenance from growth purchases; then rerun the anchor if any mismatch exists.

audit_findings.title: Unbilled end-of-lease revenue creates a working-capital requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: The balance increased $3.6m, from $69.6m to $73.2m, equal to 2.5% of the $142.7m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted increase in normalized unbilled receivables would overstate owner earnings and the cash available to equity, particularly in growth scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: Unbilled receivables related to end-of-lease services, which consists of dismantle and return delivery of buildings, were $ 73.2 million at December 31, 2025 and $ 69.6 million at December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The receivable stock is substantial, but only its normalized change enters owner earnings. The filed 2025 increase was $3.6m, which is small relative to the anchor and to the gap between the $96.24 bull value and the $111.59 market price. On the supplied evidence, it is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion, although treatment should still be verified.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the 2025 owner-earnings reconciliation includes the $3.6m increase and matching deferred service costs and collections; model normalized incremental working capital explicitly if future growth materially exceeds the historical change.
